historic/u3e1/fort-pitt-plan.jpg.description: 1759 plan of Fort Pitt, where British officers distributed smallpox-infected blankets in 1763.

historic/u3e1/royal-proclamation-1763-do.description: Printed text of the Royal Proclamation of 1763 establishing British administration, reserving lands west of the Appalachians for Native nations and requiring license for trade - London's triage to avoid another costly frontier war.

historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..description: Portrait of George Grenville (1712-1770) by William Hoare, 1764. Prime Minister 1763-1765, author of the Stamp Act.
historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..fallback_note: Wikimedia Special:FilePath -> direct upload.wikimedia.org -> NYPL (different host) -> Commons redirect
historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..used_for: George Grenville intro (t04-t05), his "brutally simple" math

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-map.jpg.description: Map showing the Proclamation Line of 1763 running along the Appalachian Mountains. German-labeled version; the red line is the visual point.
historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-map.jpg.used_for: Proclamation Line of 1763 - the line along Appalachians

historic/u3e1/french-indian-war.jpg.description: George Washington at the Battle of the Monongahela (1755) — the costly war that left Britain deeply in debt.
historic/u3e1/french-indian-war.jpg.used_for: French and Indian War debt, "won the war and emptied the treasury"

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-1763-map.description: Thomas Kitchin 1763 map 'A new map of the British Dominions in North America' showing limits settled by Proclamation October 7th 1763 - the Appalachian crest line that was to be the fence and Indian Reserve.

historic/u3e1/paxton-boys.jpg.description: The Paxton Boys marching on Philadelphia, 1764, after their 1763 attacks on Conestoga Indians.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke.jpg.description: Edmund Burke, who coined the phrase 'salutary neglect' in his 1775 speech on conciliation with America.

historic/u3e1/chief-pontiac-portrait.jpg.description: Portrait of Pontiac, Ottawa war chief around the Great Lakes who organized the 1763 pan-Indian alliance after the French defeat, distinct from Delaware prophet Neolin whose vision urged rejecting guns, alcohol, and infighting.

historic/u3e1/jeffrey-amherst-1785.jpg.description: Portrait of General Jeffrey Amherst by Thomas Gainsborough 1785 - ordered end of French gift diplomacy and cut off ceremonies, trigger for Pontiac's alliance, associated with smallpox blanket orders.

historic/u3e1/thomas-gage-1768.jpg.description: Portrait of General Thomas Gage by John Singleton Copley c.1768, commander-in-chief who replaced Amherst August 1763 and broke Pontiac's siege campaign.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke-1769.jpg.description: Portrait of Edmund Burke by studio of Sir Joshua Reynolds c.1767-1769, who coined term 'salutary neglect' in 1775 speech looking back at century of loose enforcement ended in 1763.

historic/u3e1/siege-of-fort-detroit-1763.description: Contemporary illustration 'Siege of Fort Detroit' - first target of Pontiac's alliance May 1763, shows how French forts became symbols of British occupation after gift diplomacy ended.

historic/u3e1/death-of-wolfe-west-1770.j.description: Benjamin West, 'The Death of General Wolfe' (1770): Wolfe dying at Quebec, 1759, the emblem of Britain's victory in the Seven Years' War.
historic/u3e1/death-of-wolfe-west-1770.j.verified_note: Original-file URL and size from the Commons API; image checked visually.

historic/u3e1/amherst-reynolds.jpg.description: Sir Joshua Reynolds, portrait of Jeffery Amherst, British commander-in-chief in North America after the Seven Years' War.
historic/u3e1/amherst-reynolds.jpg.verified_note: Original-file URL and size from the Commons API; image checked visually.

historic/u3e1/monongahela-stearns-print..description: Engraving after Junius Brutus Stearns, 'Life of George Washington: The Soldier': Washington at the Battle of the Monongahela, 1755 (Rijksmuseum RP-P-1905-3057).
historic/u3e1/monongahela-stearns-print..verified_note: Original-file URL and size from the Commons API; image checked visually.

historic/u3e1/pontiac-gladwin-council.jp.description: 19th-century engraving: Pontiac and Native leaders visit Major Henry Gladwin at Detroit, 1763 (the council before the siege).
historic/u3e1/pontiac-gladwin-council.jp.verified_note: Original-file URL and size from the Commons API; image checked visually.

historic/u3e1/british-grenadiers-morier..description: British grenadiers of the 16th and 17th Regiments of Foot in 1751, by David Morier, from the Royal Collection: the professional army London kept in America.

historic/u3e1/death-of-pontiac.jpg.description: The death of Pontiac, by De Cost Smith: the Ottawa war chief assassinated in 1769, six years after his 1763 rebellion.

historic/u3e1/george-iii-coronation.jpg.description: George III in his coronation robes, by Allan Ramsay; the king whose government drew the Proclamation Line.

historic/u3e1/grenville-hoare-full.jpg.description: George Grenville by William Hoare: the prime minister whose Stamp Act provoked the crisis.

historic/u3e1/lotter-pennsylvania-1756.j.description: 1756 Lotter map of eastern Pennsylvania, the colony where the Paxton Boys marched on Philadelphia in 1764.

historic/u3e1/monongahela-battle-sketch..description: Sketch of the Monongahela battlefield of 1755, where Washington first served as a colonial officer in the French and Indian War.

historic/u3e1/paxton-massacre.jpg.description: Depiction of the Paxton Boys' 1763 attack on the peaceful Conestoga Indians in Pennsylvania.

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-de.jpg.description: Map of the Proclamation Line of 1763: the boundary London drew to avoid another war.

historic/u3e1/quebec-proclamation-map.jp.description: 1763 map of the Province of Quebec as defined by the Royal Proclamation, from the Library of Congress.

historic/u3e1/quebec-proclamation-map2.j.description: Map of the Province of Quebec according to the Royal Proclamation of October 7, 1763, from the French surveys.

historic/u3e1/quebec-province-1763.jpg.description: 1763 map of the Province of Quebec, newly British after the war and governed under the Proclamation.

historic/u3e1/river-of-ohio.jpg.description: The River of Ohio, from the Library of Congress: the river valley at the heart of the post-1763 disputes.

historic/u3e1/seven-years-war-map.jpg.description: Contemporary French map of the Seven Years' War in North America, the war whose debt drove London's post-1763 tax policy.

historic/u3e1/shepherd-british-colonies..description: Shepherd's 1923 historical map of the British colonies, 1763-1776, showing the Proclamation Line era.

historic/u3e1/thomas-gage-copley.jpg.description: Thomas Gage, who replaced Amherst in August 1763 and broke Pontiac's Rebellion, painted by John Singleton Copley.

historic/u3e1/washington-virginia-colone.description: George Washington as a young Virginia colonel in 1772, already speculating in western lands and resenting crown limits on westward movement.

historic/u3e1/western-parts-map.jpg.description: Map of the western parts of Virginia, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and North Carolina, comprehending the Ohio River, from the Library of Congress.
